description: Avoid single-character variable names — they hurt readability
Use consistent naming conventions (snake_case for Python; camelCase for JavaScript)
Keep functions under 30 lines — extract helper functions for clarity
Remove commented-out code before merging — use version control instead
Cache repeated database lookups inside the request loop
Add pagination for any endpoint that returns unbounded lists
Avoid N+1 query patterns — use batch fetches or JOINs
Use database indexes for columns used in WHERE and ORDER BY clauses
Prefer async I/O for external API calls to avoid blocking the event loop
Never interpolate raw user input directly into SQL queries — use parameterized queries
Always validate that the authenticated user owns the requested resource
Do not log personally identifiable information (PII) such as emails or phone numbers
Avoid returning raw database errors to the client — use generic error messages
Store secrets in environment variables or a secret manager — never hardcode them
Validate and sanitize all user input on the server side — do not trust client validation alone
Write tests for both happy path and error scenarios
Test authorization — verify that users cannot access other users' data
Add edge-case tests for empty inputs; null values; and boundary conditions
Mock external dependencies in unit tests to ensure isolation
Assert specific values — avoid generic assertTrue without meaningful conditions
Separate request validation; business logic; and data access into distinct layers
Use descriptive variable and function names that convey intent
Avoid deep nesting — use early returns or guard clauses
Follow the Single Responsibility Principle — each function should do one thing
Remove unused imports and dead code before merging
